name: White Cliffs of Dover
text: The White Cliffs of Dover are the region of English coastline facing the Strait of Dover and France. The cliff face, which reaches a height of 350 feet (110 m), owes its striking appearance to its composition of chalk accented by streaks of black flint, deposited during the Late Cretaceous. The cliffs, on both sides of the town of Dover in Kent, stretch for eight miles (13 km).

depictions.name: White Cliffs of Dover
depictions.text: The White Cliffs of Dover, also called the Dover Cliffs, is a region of the English coastline, renowned for its striking cliffs of chalk, which were made up of countless trillions of coccoliths.
